Smashed cucumber, avocado & edamame crunch bowl

Smashed cucumbers paired with edamame for a refreshing, high-texture bowl. Smashing the cucumber helps it absorb the dressing immediately. Serve immediately after tossing for maximum crunch.

Prep
12 min prep
Total / resting
12 min total
Ingredients & Method ↓

Development edition · Awaits kitchen testing.

Ingredients Method Storage

Ingredients

How many people?
2

Estimated to serve 2 people as a comforting meal.

  • 4 (300.0 g) Persian mini cucumbers
  • 1 cup (150.0 g) shelled edamame, thawed
  • 1 ripe avocado, diced
  • 2 scallions, thinly sliced
  • 1 tbsp tamari or low-sodium soy sauce
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame oil
  • 1 tbsp rice vinegar
  • ½ tsp grated fresh ginger
  • 1 tsp maple syrup or honey
  • 1 tbsp toasted sesame seeds

Contains soy (tamari/edamame) and sesame (oil/seeds).

Method

BEFORE YOU BEGIN

If using frozen shelled edamame, thaw them by rinsing under warm water for 2 minutes and draining well.

01

Smash the cucumbers.

Place cucumbers on a cutting board. Use the flat side of a heavy chef knife or rolling pin to firmly smack them until split lengthwise. Cut diagonally into bite-sized jagged pieces.

02

Whisk dressing.

In a small bowl, whisk together tamari, toasted sesame oil, rice vinegar, grated ginger, and maple syrup until emulsified.

03

Combine bowl ingredients.

In a mixing bowl, toss smashed cucumbers, thawed edamame, and sliced scallions with the vinaigrette until well coated.

Look for: Cucumbers are well coated and slightly softened by the dressing.

04

Fold avocado and garnish.

Gently fold in diced avocado so it stays intact. Divide into portions, scatter toasted sesame seeds over top, and serve immediately.

Serve with

Can be served over cold cooked soba noodles, brown rice, or crisp gem lettuce leaves for a heartier meal. Estimated to serve 2 people as a comforting meal.

One way to change it up

Add cold cubed firm tofu for extra protein. Swap rice vinegar for fresh lime juice if you prefer a sharper citrus punch.

A small technique note

Smashing cucumbers fractures their cell walls and creates jagged edges, soaking up the ginger-sesame dressing ten times faster than clean slices.

Storage & Prep ahead

Keep at 40°F (4°C) or colder. Refrigerate within 2 hours of preparation, or within 1 hour above 90°F (32°C). Discard if left out longer. Storage life depends on ingredient freshness and preparation.
